questions.question: Two loudspeakers driven by one signal generator (160 Hz) are in phase. Explain why students hear a loud sound at point O.
questions.answer: Waves from both speakers arrive at O in phase (path difference is a whole number of wavelengths), so they reinforce: constructive interference.
steps: Both loudspeakers are driven by the same signal generator, so they are coherent and emit in phase.
At O the path lengths from the two speakers differ by a whole number of wavelengths (including zero).
Waves arriving with zero phase difference superpose, so their displacements add.
The resultant amplitude is a maximum, so the sound is loud at O.

questions.question: Explain one reason why a microphone connected to an oscilloscope gives much less uncertainty than students walking along XY.

A microphone converts the sound into an electrical signal whose size depends on the pressure amplitude.
The oscilloscope displays this signal, so the amplitude can be read precisely at each position.
The position of minimum amplitude is therefore found with much less uncertainty.

steps: Sound reflects from walls, the ceiling and the floor of a classroom.
Reflected waves travel different path lengths and superpose with the direct waves.
This changes the pattern of loud and quiet zones, so the minimum positions no longer match the direct-wave geometry.
The results are therefore unreliable; an open space avoids these reflections.

questions.question: Using Huygens construction, explain how diffraction occurs as laser light passes through a small circular gap.
questions.answer: Each point of the wavefront at the gap acts as a source of secondary wavelets, which spread into the region behind the gap so the wave bends round the edge.
steps: Huygens: every point on a wavefront acts as a source of secondary spherical wavelets.
At the gap only the wavefront points inside the opening pass the wave through.
The secondary wavelets spread out into the region behind the gap, forming a new, curved wavefront.
Diffraction is significant when the gap width is comparable to the wavelength.

Lowering the generator frequency does not change the tension or mu.
Since v = f lambda and v is constant, a lower frequency gives a longer wavelength.

questions.question: Sounds of 880 Hz and 882 Hz are produced. The ear hears frequencies differing by less than 0.3 percent as the same. Show that they are heard as the same frequency.
questions.answer: The difference of 2 Hz is 0.23 percent of 880 Hz, less than 0.3 percent, so they are heard as one frequency.
steps: Frequency difference = 882 Hz - 880 Hz = 2 Hz.
Percentage difference = 2 / 880 x 100 = 0.227 percent.
0.227 percent is less than the 0.3 percent threshold, so the ear cannot resolve the two frequencies.
Therefore the sounds are heard as the same frequency.

questions.question: When 880 Hz and 882 Hz are heard together, loudness rises and falls repeatedly. Explain why, referring to coherence and phase difference.
questions.answer: The two sources differ slightly in frequency, so they are not coherent: their phase difference changes steadily, so they reinforce and cancel in turn, giving beats at 2 Hz.
steps: The two sounds differ in frequency by 2 Hz, so their phase difference is not constant; they are not coherent.
The phase difference between the two waves at the ear changes steadily with time.
When the waves are in phase they superpose constructively, giving a loud sound.
When they are in antiphase they superpose destructively, giving a quiet sound.
The loudness therefore varies at the beat frequency f1 - f2 = 2 Hz.
Loud maxima occur twice every second.

questions.question: Lowest humming frequency is 280 Hz. Road mass 140 x 10^6 kg is supported equally by 500 cables of lengths 3.5 m to 160 m, mu = 24 kg m-1. Deduce whether the lowest-frequency standing waves on the cables could produce the hum.
questions.answer: No. The lowest (fundamental) frequencies of the cables lie between about 1 Hz and 48 Hz, so none can give 280 Hz.
steps: Tension in each cable: T = (140 x 10^6 kg / 500) x 9.81 = 2.75 x 10^6 N.

So the lowest frequencies of all the cables lie between about 1 Hz and 48 Hz.
280 Hz is outside this range, so the lowest-frequency standing waves cannot produce the hum.

questions.question: Light from a laser is coherent. State what is meant by coherent.
questions.answer: Waves have the same frequency (wavelength) and a constant phase difference between them.
steps: Coherent waves have the same frequency.
They also maintain a constant phase difference over time.
Only coherent waves produce stable interference patterns.
Because the laser light is coherent, the incident and reflected light can interfere.

questions.question: Laser light is incident at 90 deg on a reflective surface. State why a standing wave forms between the laser and the surface.
questions.answer: The incident and reflected waves have the same frequency and travel in opposite directions, so they superpose to form a standing wave.
steps: Light travels from the laser to the surface and is reflected straight back along the same path.
The incident and reflected waves have the same frequency and travel in opposite directions.
They superpose, forming nodes and antinodes at fixed positions.
The reflected wave returns along the same path, so the two waves are exactly opposed in direction.

questions.question: Describe how a stationary wave is formed inside a tube closed at one end, with a vibrating tuning fork near the open end.
questions.answer: Sound from the fork travels into the tube, reflects at the closed end and superposes with the incident wave; resonance gives a stationary wave with a node at the closed end and an antinode at the open end.
steps: The tuning fork produces longitudinal sound waves that enter the tube through the open end.
The waves travel down the tube and reflect at the closed end, where the air cannot move, so it is a displacement node.
Incident and reflected waves of the same frequency and amplitude superpose in opposite directions.
At the open end the air can move freely, so there is an antinode there.
The waves reinforce when the tube length is an odd number of quarter wavelengths: L = (2n - 1) lambda / 4.
At this resonant frequency the air column vibrates strongly in a stationary wave and the sound is loud.

Using this longer length in f = v / (4L) gives a lower frequency than the calculated value.

questions.question: Light is a transverse wave. State what is meant by a transverse wave.

questions.question: Explain how a first order maximum is produced on the screen.
questions.answer: Light diffracts at each line; at the first order angle the path difference between neighbouring lines is one wavelength, so the waves are in phase and interfere constructively.

questions.question: Explain why the graph of f squared against T is a straight line with gradient 1 / (4 l^2 mu) (same mode and length l).
questions.answer: f^2 = (n^2 / 4 l^2 mu) T, so f^2 is directly proportional to T; the line passes through the origin and its gradient is n^2 / (4 l^2 mu), a constant for fixed mode, length and mu.
steps: For the same shape of standing wave the mode n and length l are fixed.
Wave speed v = sqrt(T / mu), and v = f lambda with lambda = 2l / n.
So f = (n / 2l) sqrt(T / mu), and squaring gives f^2 = (n^2 / 4 l^2 mu) T.
Since l, mu and n are constant, f^2 is directly proportional to T, giving a straight line through the origin.
